transcript: Meeting header: 2025-07-09 15:00 PDT | Duration: ~55 mins | Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Sofia Zhang (Redwood SE), Evan Morris (Lumina Head of Security), Priya Singh (Lumina Compliance), Ryan Cole (Lumina CTO)
[00:00:00] Jordan Patel: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. Quick audio check?
[00:00:05] Evan Morris: Audio's good, thanks. We're set on time, we have about an hour, Priya and I will jump in on controls questions.

[00:00:18] Jordan Patel: Great. The goal today is to walk through our SOC 2 / ISO posture, share what we can in the Trust Center, and map controls to your requirements. Sofia will cover the technical pieces.
[00:00:30] Sofia Zhang: Hey all, yeah i'll go through encryption, KMS, RBAC and audit logs. I'll keep it high level then dive into specifics as needed.
[00:00:42] Priya Singh: Perfect. We have some mandatory questions from our audit team around scope of SOC 2 and iso, especially around data residency for EU PHI-esque data.
[00:00:55] Ryan Cole: Also want to understand differences if we go Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private in terms of control scope and encryption key ownership.

[00:01:08] Jordan Patel: Good callouts. Briefly — SOC 2 Type II covers our hosted service as run in Redwood's cloud, scope includes ingest, storage, serving for production. ISO 27001 covers our info sec mgmt system broadly. We'll share the actual reports post-call.
[00:01:26] Evan Morris: When you say 'hosted service', does that include backups and logs? Our compliance needs audit log retention and proof-of-logs for e-discovery.

[00:01:36] Sofia Zhang: Yes, logs for the hosted API are part of the system scope. We retain audit trails per our retention policy; standard retention is 90 days in the console but we can export to your log sinks longer term — S3, BigQuery, or self-hosted SIEM.
[00:01:52] Priya Singh: 90 days is borderline for us; regulators expect 1 year for certain records. Do you provide log export automation?

[00:02:00] Sofia Zhang: We do. There's a plugin and API to push logs — sometimes customers push to their cloud account for long term retention. For Dedicated or Private deployments, retention is customer-configurable and logs can stay in your environment.
[00:02:18] Ryan Cole: Ok that helps. On encryption, do you support customer-managed keys? We need KMS control for data at rest and for KV cache encryption if we host locally.

[00:02:29] Sofia Zhang: Yes. For Private we support KMS/HSM in-customer via your cloud KMS. For Dedicated we offer an option for customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key) — we can provide details in the Trust Center. Hosted API supports server-side encryption with provider-managed keys by default, and CMK for enterprise customers behind a contract.
[00:02:48] Evan Morris: Is there a split between metadata and content encryption? Our team wants to ensure embeddings and chat transcripts are encrypted in a way that prevents operator access.
[00:02:56] Jordan Patel: Good question. Sofia?

[00:02:59] Sofia Zhang: Short answer: content is encrypted at rest. Metadata might have limited plaintext for routing and quota. For sensitive workloads, Private deployment or Dedicated with CMK is recommended because audit/control surface is tighter.
[00:03:15] Priya Singh: For SOC 2 auditors we need mapping: which control IDs map to Redwood controls. Do you have a controls matrix?

[00:03:22] Jordan Patel: Yes, we maintain a controls mapping in the Trust Center — we can export a spreadsheet mapped to common frameworks (SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA). I'll get Sofia to attach the spreadsheet and pre-fill the rows that are Redwood responsibilities.
[00:03:38] Priya Singh: Great. Also need evidence for certain controls — e.g., change management, patching, incident response runbooks. Will you provide evidence packages?

[00:03:47] Jordan Patel: We provide an evidence package for enterprise customers — it includes policies, patch reports, incident response summaries, and our SOC 2 Type II report that has testing procedures. We'll redact as needed — there's an NDA path for sensitive artifacts.
[00:04:01] Evan Morris: Any gotchas — like if we use embeddings for PHI, does that change scope?

[00:04:08] Sofia Zhang: If PHI is present, it's about data classification and ensuring your contract and DPA covers PHI. Technically we can support it, but recommend Private deployment for the strongest segregation and customer KMS.
[00:04:20] Ryan Cole: On RBAC and SSO, we use Okta and expect SCIM provisioning. Does Redwood integrate?
[00:04:27] Sofia Zhang: Yes Okta + SAML SSO + SCIM for user provisioning. RBAC is role-based with admin/operator/auditor roles. We log changes to roles and provisioning events in the audit trail.
[00:04:40] Priya Singh: Do you do annual access reviews or can we trigger access certifications?
[00:04:46] Jordan Patel: We can provide a report of active users and roles for audits. For enterprise we can automate exports on a schedule — we'll add that to the actions.
[00:04:56] Evan Morris: Trust Center access — what's included?

[00:05:01] Jordan Patel: Trust Center includes SOC 2 Type II report, ISO 27001 certificate, our policies, penetration test summaries (redacted), controls mapping, and security whitepapers. Some items require an NDA to download; we'll send the link and indicate which require NDA.
[00:05:16] Priya Singh: Please mark which items require NDA. Also we need to see historical incident response timelines for the past 12 months.
[00:05:24] Jordan Patel: Incident summaries are in the Trust Center; detailed artifacts may be under NDA. We'll send examples and high-level timelines.

[00:05:32] Sofia Zhang: Technical note on audit logs — logs are writen to append-only store; we support signed log export and retention configuration. For compliance we'll show how to export to your SIEM with delivery guarantees (at-least-once delivery, retry logic).
[00:05:46] Evan Morris: Good. On data residency — we operate EU regions; does SOC 2 cover EU instances?

[00:05:54] Jordan Patel: SOC 2 tests are across our production services; region-specific hosting is available via separate deployment options. For true EU residency we recommend Dedicated in EU region or Private. We'll note that the hosted SOC 2 artifacts primarily reflect our global controls, not per-region infrastructure certificates.
[00:06:12] Ryan Cole: So if we need all customer data to remain in EU, Hosted might not be ok?

[00:06:17] Sofia Zhang: Hosted can be routed to EU region, but for regulatory guarantees Dedicated/Private is the stronger option since you control networking and key management. We'll provide a comparison doc.
[00:06:28] Priya Singh: On encryption in transit, TLS versions and ciphers — do you support TLS 1.3?
[00:06:33] Sofia Zhang: Yes, TLS 1.3 for all external endpoints, and internal service-to-service uses mTLS. Cipher suites are aligned with modern recommendations.
[00:06:44] Evan Morris: Is there separation between operator and platform admin? We need to ensure no developer can access customer plaintext without proper authorization.

[00:06:51] Sofia Zhang: We enforce least privilege, RBAC, and privileged access management for ops. Access to customer data is audited and requires justification and approval. For sensitive workloads we recommend Private so you can retain full control.
[00:07:05] Jordan Patel: Quick pause — any blockers so far?
[00:07:08] Priya Singh: The primary blockers are: we need SOC 2 evidence, controls mapping, and clarity on log retention automation. Also legal wants to see DPA with KMS clauses.
[00:07:17] Jordan Patel: Understood — that'll be in the next steps. Sofia, can you run through mapping example for a couple of controls?

[00:07:23] Sofia Zhang: Sure. Example: CC6 (change management) — our controls include PR review, CI/CD gated deploys, automated vulnerability scans; evidence is deploy logs and scan reports. Another: CC7 (logical access) — RBAC, SSO, periodic reviews. I'll add the specific doc links in the spreadsheet.
[00:07:45] Evan Morris: Sounds good. For auditors we also need to know if you engage third-party penetration testers and how frequently.
[00:07:51] Jordan Patel: We do annual pen tests plus continuous triage via bug bounty and external scanning. Summaries are in Trust Center, full reports under NDA.
[00:07:59] Ryan Cole: On the topic of KV caches — we run heavy inference internally, any chance to see perf implications of enabling CMK for KV cache?

[00:08:07] Sofia Zhang: There's a small perf delta when doing envelope encryption with external KMS calls for each cache write; we recommend envelope keys and caching of DEKs to minimize latency. We'll run a short benchmark and share numbers specific to EU region as requested.
[00:08:24] Priya Singh: Could you note that in the controls mapping as a risk/mitigation for latency?
[00:08:29] Sofia Zhang: Yep, will include technical tradeoffs and recommended configs.
[00:08:36] Jordan Patel: Let's talk about evidence handoff: we'll share reports, and Sofia will pre-fill controls mapping. Priya, do you want a separate legal thread for NDA/DPA?
[00:08:45] Priya Singh: Yes, legal will take the NDA path for detailed artifacts. I'll loop in our counsel after today's meeting.
[00:08:52] Evan Morris: For the audit log retention automation — can you provide an example config for pushing to S3 with server-side encryption and S3 lifecycle for 1 year?
[00:08:59] Sofia Zhang: Absolutely — I'll attach sample config and a runbook for log export, including S3 SSE-KMS configuration.
[00:09:09] Ryan Cole: One last technical: do you have SOC 2 scoping guidance for data processors vs controllers? We need language for contracts.
[00:09:16] Jordan Patel: We have standard clauses in the DPA; we'll share recommended language and highlight where Redwood is processor. Legal can tweak based on your legal team's needs.
[00:09:25] Priya Singh: Great. Any customers with similar regulatory profiles you can share references for?
[00:09:30] Jordan Patel: We can share anonymized references in healthcare and regulated SaaS — will include a couple of sketched use-cases in the follow-up email.
[00:09:38] Evan Morris: Ok let's capture next steps now.

[00:09:42] Jordan Patel: Action recap: Jordan send SOC2 + ISO cert; Sofia send Trust Center link, controls mapping spreadsheet, log export runbook and KV cache perf notes; Priya to send residency/retention requirements; Ryan to provide infra contact. Schedule legal follow-up and technical deep-dive next week. Any additions?
[00:09:59] Priya Singh: No, that's everything from compliance side. Thank you.
[00:10:03] Ryan Cole: Thanks all, we'll review the artifacts and be ready for the next call.
[00:10:09] Jordan Patel: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up by email with the artifacts and proposed times for follow-ups. Meeting end.
[00:10:15] End of transcript (auto-exported). Note: transcription may contain inaccuracies; detailed artifacts will be provided as PDF/links.
